conviction_note: Near-balanced: the company reaffirmed Modern Oral sales and cut the EBITDA guide on 2026-09-21 with nine days of Q3 left, so the quarter probably lands inside a guide the market already marked down 10% for. Against that sit a competitor price cut (ZYN moving to 20-pouch cans, about 25% less revenue per pouch, Q4 'abnormally low' US profit) that bears on TPB's Q4 and 2027 pricing, counterparty data showing the pouch incumbents losing share to challengers, about 16-17% of shares sold short at 6.7 days to cover, and the new CEO's first call. Findings sum to +0.40 and the scaled number is +0.44 (p_up 52 x abs 11); the two agree because nothing found is decisive.
bar: Revenue $147.05m, consensus EPS $0.33 non-GAAP (whisper $0.32) per Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/TPB, read 2026-11-06). EPS sources disagree: a Benzinga search snippet gives Q3 '26 $0.31 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TPB/earnings-forecasts, page 403 on fetch) and the sweep row records an earlier $0.19. The company bar is FY2026 Modern Oral net sales of $260-270m and adjusted EBITDA of $70-80m, reaffirmed/narrowed on 2026-09-21 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1290677/000143774926030820/ex_1018072.htm). H1 Modern Oral net was $52.0m + $68.4m = $120.4m, so the guide implies H2 of $139.6-149.6m, about $70-75m a quarter against Q2's $68.4m; non-MO sales were $74.5m in Q2, so $147m revenue is consistent with the guide midpoint. The revenue bar has one estimate source, so reported-quarter findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 3.24M shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, 6.7 days to cover on 482k average volume, against 19.37M shares outstanding, i.e. about 16.7% of shares outstanding (massive.com quote page, as of 2026-11-04: https://massive.com/quote/tpb). The 2026-09-30 settlement was 3.18M at 5.8 days, so the position is steady to rising. Benzinga's sentiment page shows 15.1% of float short, undated, labelled 'Rising' (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/TPB/sentiment). That is a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d_vol_points is null, so the option market makes no directional statement. Put/call OI is 0.57 on only 221 contracts, the ATM spread is 63% of mid, and the implied move of 12.4% is indicative only. The tape: +20.8% over one month to the 2026-11-04 close of $70.40 off an October low of $54.17, then down to $65.66 by 2026-11-06 (run_up_5d -2.45%, 20d +14.44%), 54% below the 52-week high. AAII: two upgrades and no downgrades in the month to 2026-11-05.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21, with nine days of Q3 left, TPB reaffirmed FY2026 Modern Oral gross sales of $330-350m and net sales of $260-270m and cut adjusted EBITDA to $70-80m from $70-90m, citing prolonged higher freight and no onshoring margin benefit until 2027. The MO guide implies H2 net of $139.6-149.6m (about $70-75m a quarter against Q2's $68.4m, which was +32% q/q). A company that could see almost all of Q3 chose not to raise, so the Q3 MO number most likely lands inside the guide and the consensus of about $147m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell about 10% on the 2026-09-21 release (CEO exit plus EBITDA cut; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-turning-point-brands-stock-dived-10-today). At Q2 (2026-08-04), an MO guide raised by about $50m with EBITDA held bought only +2.56%. At Q4 2025 (2026-03-02) the 2026 EBITDA investment guide cost -20.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the stock took the EBITDA cut on 2026-09-21. What is not settled is how far inside the reaffirmed MO range Q3 lands. If the market expected a beat-and-raise on MO momentum, the October +20% rally would sit on a bar the company implicitly declined to lift.
findings.independence: The consensus revenue of $147.05m (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/TPB) is consistent with the guide midpoint, but analysts derive it from the guide, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: PMI's Q3 2026 release (week before 2026-10-26) says it is moving most ZYN flagship cans from 15 to 20 pouches, about 25% less revenue per pouch, and expects 'an abnormally low level of U.S. profitability' in Q4 as an investment quarter. The category leader is cutting its effective price as TPB goes into chain resets (ALP into fall resets, chain store count +70% by year-end). That pressures FRE/ALP pricing and gross-to-net in Q4 and 2027, which TPB's call will be asked about.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TPB's largest negative reaction in the baseline (-20.79%, 2026-03-02) came on margin and investment guidance for Modern Oral, not on the reported quarter. Management said on the Q2 call that the promotional environment was 'similar to the spring' and expected it to continue into Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for about two weeks, yet TPB rallied about 20% through late October, which suggests holders are not discounting a pricing response. If it were priced, TPB would have sold off on the PMI release date and estimates for Q4 MO net sales would have come down. Neither is visible, and two upgrades came in the month.
findings.independence: Altria Q3 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764180/000076418026000112/exhibit991erq32026.htm) shows on! shipments +13.3% with retail-share pressure, a competitive category. Same theme, different company. Shrunk from -1.5 for the crowded short.

findings.finding: Counterparties that reported after TPB last spoke show the pouch incumbents growing slower than the category. ZYN US shipments rose only 4.2% to 3.2bn pouches in Q3 2026 (PMI). Altria's Q3 10-Q has pouches at 59.8% of US oral, +7.6 points, with on! share of the pouch category down 2.3 points (secondary summary of the 10-Q). Share is moving to challengers, consistent with TPB MO volume momentum. Net of the rest of the company: MO is about 48% of sales, while Zig-Zag (25%, -24.8% y/y in Q2) and heritage Stoker's (-1% y/y) are flat to falling.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MO beats have been bought on this name: +11.03% on 2026-05-07 (MO guide raised to $210-225m) and +2.56% on 2026-08-04 (raised to $260-270m).
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry read, not TPB's number, and the reaffirmed guide on 2026-09-21 already embeds TPB's own view of Q3. If the category shift were fully transmitted, the MO guide would have been raised in September. It may instead show up as Q3 MO at the top of the implied $70-75m run-rate.
findings.independence: Altria Q3 2026 release and 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764180/000076418026000114/mo-20260930.htm), a different counterparty. A proxy for TPB volume, not confirmed by TPB.

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call under new CEO David Glazek (Executive Chairman since 2023, ex-Standard General/Lazard, effective 2026-10-01). Graham Purdy left abruptly on 2026-09-18 for 'personal reasons'. A new CEO's first print is when a reset (spend, 2027 framing, Louisville plant timing, which was 'by year-end subject to regulatory approval' on the Q2 call) or a strategic message is most likely. The direction is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition print for this CEO. The 2026-09-21 announcement itself cost about 10%. Guide-driven prints on this name have moved -20.8% and +24.8% (2025-05-07).
findings.why_not_priced: It is not a directional fact. It raises the variance of the guide line, which is why abs_move_pct is set above the history median rather than below it. If the market priced a kitchen-sink reset, the stock would not have rallied 20% in October.
findings.independence: Q2 call commentary on the Louisville plant (https://www.webull.com/news/15344824567096320) is the other open item a new CEO would address.

findings.finding: Short interest is 3.24M shares (2026-10-15), about 16.7% of 19.37M shares outstanding, at 6.7 days to cover, up from 3.18M/5.8 days on 2026-09-30. Any clean MO beat or reassurance on pricing meets a crowded short in a name trading about 480k shares a day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 of the last 8 prints were up, with three of the up moves above 11% (+11.0, +14.2, +24.8), consistent with a short base that covers on good MO numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: The October rally to $70 may have been partly covering, but short interest rose into mid-October rather than falling. If the short had covered, days to cover would be falling, and it went from 5.8 to 6.7.
findings.independence: Benzinga sentiment shows 15.1% of float short, 'Rising' (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/TPB/sentiment), a different data vendor.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 included an out-of-period IEEPA tariff refund ($8.5m adjusted out of EBITDA, $0.31 per share out of adjusted EPS, $18m FCF benefit). Refunds on liquidated entries are still being processed, so Q3 may carry another out-of-period credit. It would be a one-off that the company adjusts out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 refund print moved +2.56% while the refund was stripped from adjusted numbers. No sign the refund itself moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is adjusted out of the metrics the stock trades on and has no path to the guide, so it is worth a fraction of its dollars. GAAP EPS could optically beat.
findings.independence: IEEPA refund process status (https://www.cato.org/blog/us-tariff-refunds-mostly-good-developments-still-long-way-go), a macro proxy only. Management did not mention further refunds on the Q2 call.

findings.finding: The stock ran +20.8% in the month to 2026-11-04 (October low $54.17 to $70.40) on two analyst upgrades and no downgrades, then gave back about 7% to $65.66 into the print. The bar for 'reassurance' is higher than at the October low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's 20d run-up of +14.4% compares with a 2026-08-04 print that followed a weak tape and moved only +2.56%. There is no clear run-up/reaction pattern in the eight prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is small, and shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: The massive.com quote page gives the same +20.82% one-month return (https://massive.com/quote/tpb).

outside_window.finding: Louisville US pouch manufacturing launch 'by year-end subject to regulatory approval'; the Sept guide assumes no margin benefit until 2027. Actual qualification and the ~70% gross margin target resolve after the window unless the call gives a date.
Oppenheimer cut its price target to $90 from $130 (Outperform) on 2026-09-22. This is past and priced, kept only as context for where the sell-side sits.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The October run-up of +20% has been partly given back. The evidence is mixed: a competitor price cut negative, category share shift and a crowded short positive. It neither cuts strongly against the tape nor confirms it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, about 16-17% of shares, 6.7 DTC): ZYN pricing negative shrunk -1.5 to -1.0; run-up positioning negative -0.3 to -0.2
Lesson 6 (inside the guide; revenue bar from one source, EPS bar disputed): Sept-21 reaffirmation finding moved toward 0, -0.5 to -0.2
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): category share-shift finding sized net of declining Zig-Zag and flat Stoker's, +1.0 to +0.7
Lesson 2 (one-off below the line with no path to the guide): tariff refund +0.2 to +0.1
abs_move_pct and p_up left unchanged: lessons 1 and 8 argue against shrinking abs below the implied 12.4% and median 9.6%
